title: Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: According to the Rambam in his Introduction to Zera’im, he was the son of Rabbi Chanina, the Deputy of the Kohanim.
He is mentioned three times in the Mishnah, and in all of them Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel speaks in his name:
In Shekalim 8:5: the curtain was a handbreadth thick. In Ketubot 2:8: one is raised to the priesthood on the testimony of one witness.
And in Menachot 11:9: the baking of the showbread overrides a festival but not Yom Kippur.

In Keritot 6b: “The leftover incense — once every sixty [years] — the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said it in the name of the Segan”; Hyman suggests that perhaps it should read “in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben HaSegan.”

He is mentioned in Tosefta Rosh Hashanah, chapter 2: “Shimon ben HaSegan says: If witnesses came from minchah time onward, they would sound the shofar.” And in Tosefta Yoma, chapter 2: “Every day it had no nashtik (so it is in Zuckermandel’s Tosefta; see Yoma 44b), and on this day it had a nashtik — the words of Ben Segan.”
Seder HaDorot conjectures that he is Shimon bar Kahana; see his entry.

notes.text: אחת לששים is once every sixty years, not one part in sixty. Saved Davidson Keritot6b describes the accumulated leftover incense and sixty or seventy years; Hyman’s shorter sixty wording remains. נשתיק is retained as nashtik, a handle/fitting; the Ben HaSegan correction remains his proposal.

Keritot 6b directly gives once in sixty or seventy years, while Hyman abbreviates to sixty. The consulted Machon Mamre Tosefta Yoma 2 text has the bracketed form ושתיק in the Ben HaSegan fitting statement; Hyman supplies נשתיק and attributes it to Zuckermandel. That exact Zuckermandel printing and the Rambam genealogy passage were not independently inspected.
